text:
Taylor Hall played his 1,000th NHL game in November, and the Hurricanes honored him for it. The first overall pick of 2010, a Hart Trophy winner in 2017-18 and a Stanley Cup champion with Carolina last season, he is 35 now and playing a different job: 13 minutes a night in the middle of a deep lineup.

He is doing it well. Carolina takes 65% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) at five on five with him on the ice, and his 2.85 points per 60 minutes is near the top of our talent range. Ten points in 16 games, his own chances up to 1.21 expected goals per 60 from 0.90 last season. If anything, his linemates have finished a little below their chances around him. Evolving-Hockey's warning from last season still applies: he plays with strong teammates, which flatters raw on-ice numbers.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking pegged him as a setup man and a carrier at the blue line, and that is the version of Hall we see now. Watch his minutes, which have slipped to about 12 and a half over his last ten games.
